questions: Was the facial asymmetry present from birth or early infancy?
Did it begin after a sudden episode of facial weakness or paralysis?
Did the affected side ever recover partially after that episode?
Does closing one eye involuntarily pull the corner of the mouth upward or outward?
Does raising your eyebrows involuntarily narrow or close one eye?
Does smiling or chewing cause involuntary narrowing or closure of one eye?
Have you ever had facial trauma or surgery near the ear, face, or skull?
Have you ever had an infection involving the ear, face, or brain?
Have you had recurrent episodes of facial weakness?
Has the asymmetry been progressively worsening?
Do you have hearing loss, ringing in the ear, dizziness, or ear discharge on the affected side?
Do you have numbness or weakness in an arm or leg, difficulty speaking, or difficulty swallowing?
Do you have involuntary twitching of the facial muscles when the face is otherwise at rest?
Does the affected eye become dry, painful, or difficult to close completely?
Did the facial weakness occur after birth injury or a difficult delivery?

served: MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast
results: 1. Detailed cranial nerve and facial motor examination, including voluntary facial movements and synkinesis maneuvers
cranial nerve examination: bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis; narrowed left palpebral fissure
synkinesis assessment (eye closure with platysma/frontalis): co-contraction of eye closure with the left platysma and left frontalis; right lower-lip curling on speech and mastication
palpebral fissure width both sides: narrowed LEFT palpebral fissure from established synkinesis
2. Contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals
MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast: no tumour, no perineural enhancement, no central lesion
3. Facial nerve electroneurography and electromyography with blink-reflex testing
electroneuronography / facial EMG: chronic reinnervation with synkinetic co-activation; no active denervation
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis due to aberrant regeneration after recurrent idiopathic facial nerve palsy (recurrent Bell’s palsy).

ALTERNATIVE: Melkersson–Rosenthal syndrome with recurrent facial palsy.

ALTERNATIVE: Facial nerve schwannoma or other occult facial-nerve lesion.

ALTERNATIVE: Congenital facial synkinesis syndrome.
